titleEn: Book of the Dead of Ani — Spells 26 and 30B
part: Spells 26 and 30B — giving the heart; the heart not opposing (Plate 15)
about: Two short spells on Plate 15 of Ani's papyrus, both about the dead man's heart. In Spell 26 Ani is given his heart back in the necropolis, and with it the use of his mouth, legs, arms and eyes, so that he can go in and out at the gates of the West. Spell 30B is the plea written over the weighing of the heart on Plates 3–4, here with its own title: Ani asks his heart not to stand up against him as a witness before the gods. Several words in Spell 26 are rare or obscure, and the notes say where the reading is doubtful.

sentences.l: spell · of · giving · the-heart · of · the-Osiris · Ani · to-him · in · the-necropolis
sentences.i: Spell for giving the heart of the Osiris Ani to him in the necropolis.
sentences.n: Spell 26 begins. Before it, Budge prints Spell 25 from the papyrus of Nebseni; Ani's papyrus does not have that spell. The papyrus writes rꜣ n rdit ib n in red; Osiris, Ani and the rest are black. rdit 'giving' is the mouth r, the arm (D36; the print shows no loaf, so it is not the giving hand D37) and t: the infinitive of rdi. ib 'heart' is the heart sign with its stroke. The second n is taken as the genitive, 'the heart of the Osiris Ani', and n·f, water n with the viper ·f, as 'to him', the one it is given back to. Budge takes that n as 'to' and n·f as a repetition ('to Osiris Ani, to him'), and the signs allow that too. wsir is the low seat (coded Q2, approximate) over the eye, as before, and ꜣny has the squatting man with a flail (A52). ẖrt-nṯr 'the necropolis' is the flag nṯr, written first out of respect, with r and the butcher's block ẖr (T28) in one ligature, its t not written. The ib is the heart as the seat of mind and will. Without it the dead man could not think, speak or act.

sentences.l: heart-my · to-me · in · the-house · of-hearts · heart-my · to-me · in · the-house · of-hearts
sentences.i: My heart (ib) is mine in the House of Hearts; my heart (ḥꜣty) is mine in the House of Hearts.
sentences.n: Ani speaks. ib·i 'my heart' is the heart and stroke with the seated man ·i. n·i is water n with ·i. The preposition with its suffix is the predicate: 'my heart (is) to me', the Egyptian way of saying 'my heart is mine'. Without a verb the sentence could also be a wish, 'may my heart be mine'. m 'in' is the owl in the first half and the sign m (Aa15) in the second. pr 'house' is the house sign with its stroke. ibw 'hearts' is the heart with plural strokes, and pr ibw is the direct genitive, two nouns side by side, 'the House of Hearts'. The second half says the same with the other word for heart. ḥꜣty is the forepart of a lion ḥꜣt with t as complement, two strokes y and the heart as classifier. In ḥꜣtyw the strokes y are left out, and the chick w (Z7, a small coil in the print) stands after the heart, with plural strokes. ib and ḥꜣty both mean 'heart', and English cannot keep them apart. The House of Hearts is not described further: it is perhaps a place in the world below where hearts are kept.

sentences.l: (iw) · to-me · heart-my · rests-it · in-me
sentences.i: I have my heart; it rests in me.
sentences.n: Budge prints iw and n·i as one group (àu-nà). They are split here into iw, the reed and the chick, which opens a statement, and n·i 'to me'. iw n·i X is 'X is mine, I have X'. ḥtp·f 'it rests' is the offering-mat ḥtp with t and p as complements and the viper ·f: the sḏm·f, its ·f looking back to the heart. im·i 'in me' is the reed and the owl, im, the form of m before a suffix, with ·i. The seated man is restored by Budge.

sentences.l: not · shall-eat(?)-I · the-cakes · of · Osiris · on · the-side · eastern · of · Agy
sentences.i: I shall not eat(?) the cakes of Osiris on the eastern side of Agy.
sentences.n: nn is the negative arms (coded D35, approximate) with water n. nn with the sḏm·f is the negative of the future, 'I shall not …'. The verb is the crossed planks (Z11), which write im, with m as complement, the chick w, the man with hand to mouth as classifier of eating, and ·i. No verb im 'eat' is known. The word is taken, with a query, as ꜥm 'swallow, eat', which sounds much the same, and the w as the ending of the prospective sḏm·f (Budge: àmu, 'eat'). The reading is not sure. šꜥt 'cakes' is the pool š (coded N37, approximate), t, the arm ꜥ and three grains (N33) as classifier, with the t written before the arm. It is a word for a kind of bread (Budge: śetā), spelled like šꜥt 'slaughter' but a different word. nt is the feminine genitive, and wsir here is the god himself. ḥr gs iꜣbty 'on the eastern side': gs is the flat sign with a bevelled end (coded Aa13, approximate) with its stroke. iꜣbty is the emblem of the East iꜣb (R15) with b as complement, t and two strokes y: the nisba 'eastern', masculine to agree with gs. ꜣgy is the vulture ꜣ, the jar-stand g (W11) and two reeds y, with a water sign (coded N36, approximate), a strip of land (N21) and a stroke as classifiers. It names some stretch of water. Budge renders it 'the Lake of Flowers', but no flower is written, and the place is not known. Budge's numeral 3 is printed inside the word, after the reeds, and the line is kept at 2. The clause follows the one before without a link (Budge supplies 'or'), and how the two hang together is not clear.

sentences.l: a-boat(?) · in · going-downstream-your · sailing-upstream-your · not · shall-go-down-I · into · the-boat(?) · which-is-with-you
sentences.i: A boat(?) as you sail downstream and upstream: I shall not go down into the boat(?) that is with you.
sentences.n: This passage is obscure. ḫwḫt is ḫ, the chick w, ḫ again and t, with a boat (coded P1, approximate) as classifier. It is some kind of boat (Budge: χuχet), a word not met before in these parts. ḫd·k 'your going downstream' is ḫ and d with the boat and ·k: the infinitive of ḫdi with ·k as its subject. ḫnt·k 'your sailing upstream' is the rack of jars ḫnt (coded W17, approximate) with n and t, two oblique strokes (not read), a boat with a sail (P2) and ·k. The owl m is not written again before it (Budge supplies 'and in'). The text does not say who 'you' is. nn hꜣ·i 'I shall not go down' is nn with hꜣ, the courtyard h (O4), ꜣ and the walking legs (printed as a small Λ, coded D54), and ·i. r 'into'. ḫwdt is ḫ, w, d and t with the boat: another boat-word (Budge: χuṭet), perhaps the same one in another spelling. Neither word is certain. imy·k is the reed, the crossed planks im with m, two strokes y and ·k: the nisba imy 'which is in, with', with a suffix, 'which is with you' (Budge: àmi-k). How these clauses join the rest of the spell is not clear, and the rendering follows the order of the signs.

sentences.l: (iw) · to-me · mouth-my · may-speak-I · with-it · legs-my · to · walk · arms-my · to · fell · enemy-my
sentences.i: I have my mouth, that I may speak with it, my legs to walk, my arms to fell my enemy.
sentences.n: iw n·i as in line 2, split here as there. rꜣ·i 'my mouth' is the mouth with its stroke and ·i. ḏdw·i is a tall tapering sign (coded U28, approximate), the fire-drill ḏꜣ, here standing for ḏ as in Spell 23. Then come the hand d, the chick w, the man with hand to mouth and ·i: ḏd 'speak' with the w of the prospective sḏm·f, 'that I may speak'. Budge's '[that]' has no sign. im·f 'with it'. rdwy·i 'my two legs' is r and d with two legs (D56) and the walking legs as classifiers, and ·i: the dual of rd, its ending wy not written. r šmt 'to walk' is r 'to' with an infinitive. šmt is the pool on legs šm (N40), with m (Aa15) as complement, t and the walking legs. ꜥwy·i 'my two arms' is the arm with its stroke, a second arm, two strokes y, the chick w and ·i. sḫr 'fell' is the bolt s, ḫ and r, with a bowing man (coded A16, approximate) and the low hooked sign (coded U15) as classifiers: the causative of ḫr 'fall'. ḫfty·i 'my enemy' is ḫ, f and t with a kneeling enemy, one arm raised (coded A13, approximate). No seated man follows, and the stroke after the classifier is taken as the suffix ·i, which the stroke often writes. The y of ḫfty is not written (Budge: χeft-à). Mouth, legs and arms are the powers the dead man needs back in order to act in the next world.

sentences.l: are-opened · to-me · the-two-doors · of · heaven
sentences.i: The doors of heaven are opened to me.
sentences.n: Budge prints wn and n·i as one group (un-nà), split here. wn 'open' is the hare wn with n, and a door-leaf (coded O31) and the low hooked sign as classifiers, as in Spell 23. It is the passive sḏm·f, 'are opened', and it could also be a wish, 'may (they) be opened'. n·i 'to me' stands before the noun subject, as a short prepositional phrase with a pronoun does. ꜥꜣwy 'the two doors' is the door-leaf written twice: the dual of ꜥꜣ 'door, door-leaf' (Budge: āa). n pt 'of heaven'. The doors of the sky open for the dead as they open for the sun.

sentences.l: may-open · to-me · Geb · the-heir · of-the-gods · two-jaws-his · to-me
sentences.i: May Geb, the heir of the gods, open his two jaws for me.
sentences.n: Budge's one group seśu-nà is split into sšw and n·i. sšw is the bolt s, the pool š (coded N37, approximate) and the chick w, with crossed sticks (Z9) and the low hooked sign as classifiers. It is sš 'open (a door), unbolt', and the w is taken as the ending of the prospective sḏm·f, 'may (Geb) open'. gb 'Geb' is the goose gb (G38) with b and the seated god (Budge: Seb). iry-pꜥt 'the heir' is the mouth for iry with p, the arm ꜥ, t and an egg (coded H8) as classifier. It is the title of the highest noble, here given to Geb as heir of the gods (Budge: erpāt). nṯrw 'of the gods' is the flag three times, in the direct genitive. ꜥrty·f 'his two jaws' is the arm ꜥ, r and t, two strokes y for the dual, and two jawbones (F19) as classifiers. Then come t again (a complement, not read), ·f, and two strokes, which are the strokes of the dual after a suffix and are not read. r·i 'to me'. Geb is the earth in which the dead lie. When he opens his jaws, the dead man can come out.

sentences.l: may-open-he · two-eyes-my · bound(?) · may-stretch-out-he · two-legs-my · drawn-up(?)
sentences.i: May he open my eyes, which are bound(?); may he stretch out my legs, which are drawn up(?).
sentences.n: wn·f 'may he open' is wn as above with ·f: the sḏm·f as a wish, its ·f still Geb. irty·i 'my two eyes' is the eye written twice and ·i: the dual of irt 'eye' (Budge reads maa). šdntt is the pool š (coded N37, approximate), the hand d, n and t twice, with a coiled cord (coded V1, approximate) and the low hooked sign as classifiers. It is a word for eyes covered or bound (Budge: śeṭentet, 'blinded'), and the cord points to binding. It is taken as a verb in the stative, the second t belonging to its ending, which agrees with the eyes. The word is not met elsewhere in these parts, and its sense is uncertain. dwn·f 'may he stretch out' is the hand d and the hare wn, with n and w as complements, and ·f: dwn 'stretch out'. rdwy·i 'my two legs' as in line 4 (Budge's line 6 begins with it). qrfy is the hill-slope q, r, f and two reeds y, with the cord (V1, approximate) and the low hooked sign. It is taken as qrf 'be drawn together, contracted', in the stative describing the legs (Budge: qerfi, 'fastened together'), and the reading is uncertain. A mummy lies with its eyes closed and its legs bound in bandages, and the god is asked to free them.

sentences.l: making-firm · by · Anubis · knees-my · may-raise-up · for-me
sentences.i: Anubis makes my knees firm, so that they lift me up(?).
sentences.n: srwd 'make firm' is the bolt s, the causative prefix, with r, d and w written before the sign rwd (coded T12, approximate) and the roll: the causative of rwd 'be firm', the verb of Spell 24. Water n stands alone after it, with no English in Budge. It is taken as in 'by', written without its reed, bringing in the doer: srwd in inpw, 'making firm by Anubis', is an infinitive with its subject, 'Anubis makes firm'. The reading is uncertain. inpw 'Anubis' is the reed, n, p and w with the jackal-headed god (C6). mꜣsty·i is the sickle mꜣ (U1) drawn on the vulture's back in one ligature, the vulture ꜣ as complement, the bolt s (coded S29, approximate; the print looks more like a leg), t, two strokes y, two legs and the walking legs, and ·i. It is taken as the dual of mꜣst 'knee' (Budge: masti, 'legs'). ṯsw is the knot ṯs (coded S24, approximate) with s as complement, the chick w and the low hooked sign. It is ṯs 'raise, lift up' with the w of the prospective, its subject (the knees) not written, and r·i 'for me' after it. The sense is uncertain. Anubis wrapped the body, and here he gives it back the strength to stand.

sentences.l: raises-up · me · Sekhmet · the-goddess · may-be-I · in · heaven
sentences.i: Sekhmet the goddess raises me up, that I may be in heaven.
sentences.n: dwn is the hand d and the hare wn with n and the walking legs. Budge prints the chick w and the seated man with it (ṭunu-à, 'maketh me to rise'). They are split off here as wi 'me', the dependent pronoun, written with the chick and the seated man. A pronoun object stands before a noun subject, so dwn wi sḫmt is 'Sekhmet raises me up'. The group could also be read dwn·i 'I rise up', with w as a complement. sḫmt 'Sekhmet' is the sceptre sḫm (coded S42) with ḫ, t and a seated goddess (coded B1, approximate), as in Spell 23. Budge's line 7 begins with it. nṯrt 'the goddess' is the flag with t, r and t and the cobra (I12) as classifier. wnn·i 'that I may be' is the hare wn with n twice and ·i: the sḏm·f of wnn 'be' after another verb, expressing purpose. m pt 'in heaven'. Sekhmet, 'the Mighty One', is the lion goddess, and her strength lifts the dead man to the sky.

sentences.l: is-done · what-have-commanded-I · in · Memphis
sentences.i: What I have commanded is done in Memphis.
sentences.n: irw is the eye ir with the chick w: the passive sḏm·f of iri 'do', written with w, 'is done'. wḏ·n·i is the sign wḏ (V24) with w as complement and the roll, water n and ·i. It is the relative form sḏm·n·f, 'what I have commanded', and is the subject of irw (Budge prints utu-nà). The n is the n of the sḏm·n·f, not 'to me'. ḥwt-kꜣ-ptḥ 'Memphis' is one framed group: the enclosure ḥwt (O6) with p and t, the wick ḥ, a flag-like sign (coded R8, as printed) and the raised arms kꜣ (D28) inside it, and the town sign (O49) outside. The god's name is written before kꜣ out of respect. The flag is not read: it may be a god classifier after Ptah's name. It means 'the Mansion of the ka of Ptah', the name of Ptah's temple, used for his city (Budge: Ḥet-Ptaḥ-ka). To be obeyed in Memphis is to have the standing of a lord among the living.

sentences.l: know-I · in · heart-my · have-power-I · over · heart-my · have-power-I · over · arms-my · have-power-I · over · legs-my · have-power-I · over · doing · what-desires · ka-my
sentences.i: I have knowledge in my heart; I have power over my heart, I have power over my arms, I have power over my legs, I have power to do what my ka desires.
sentences.n: rḫ·i 'I know' is r and ḫ with the roll and ·i. m ib·i 'in my heart': Budge gives the owl no English, and it is taken as 'in', the heart as the seat of knowing. sḫm·i 'I have power' is the sceptre sḫm (S42) with m as complement, the low hooked sign as classifier and ·i; sḫm m is 'have power over, be master of'. The second sḫm·i, in line 8, is printed with the owl joined to a small arm (D36) where the others have the low hooked sign. It is read as the same word, with another form of the classifier. ḥꜣty·i, ꜥwy·i and rdwy·i as before. iryt 'doing' is the eye ir with two reeds y, t and the roll: the infinitive of iri, written with its weak y. mrrt 'what … desires' is the hoe mr (coded U6, approximate) with r as complement, r again, t and the man with hand to mouth. It is the imperfective relative form of mri, marked by the doubled r, and kꜣ·i 'my ka' (the raised arms, stroke and ·i) is its subject. The ka is the life-force, which lives on offerings, and to do what it desires is to live well in the next world.

sentences.l: not · shall-be-shut-in(?) · ba-my · [from] · corpse-my · [at] · the-gates · of · the-West · in · entering-my · in · peace · coming-forth · in · peace
sentences.i: My ba shall not be shut away(?) from my corpse at the gates of the West, when I go in in peace and come out in peace.
sentences.n: nn as in line 2. ḫni·tw is ḫ, n and the reed i, then a forked upright (coded O30, approximate), a small sign with a hooked tail (coded Aa2, approximate) and the low hooked sign as classifiers, t and w: the passive sḏm·tw·f. The signs give ḫni. It is taken as a writing of ḫnr 'restrain, shut in', the r written as i, but the reading is uncertain (Budge: χenà-tu, 'be imprisoned'). bꜣ·i 'my ba' is the jabiru bꜣ (G29) with ·i, and the small sign before it is coded R7 (the incense bowl), as in Spell 18, and not read. Budge prints a small tick between the bird and the seated man, not coded. r 'from' and ḥr 'at' are restored by Budge. ẖꜣt·i 'my corpse' is the belly ẖ, ꜣ and t, with an oval crossed by a line (coded Aa2, approximate) and a lying figure (coded A54, approximate) as classifiers, and ·i. sbꜣw 'the gates' is the star sbꜣ (N14) with s, b and ꜣ as complements, then w. A rod-like sign (coded T11, approximate) and the house follow as classifiers, each with plural strokes. nw is the plural genitive, the pot nw with a stroke. imntt 'the West' is the emblem of the West with t twice and the hill-country sign. m ꜥq·i is m with the infinitive ꜥq 'enter' (the cormorant ꜥq, coded G35, approximate, with q and the walking legs) and ·i as its subject: 'in my entering', 'when I enter'. prt 'coming forth' is the house pr with r, t and the walking legs, the infinitive of pri, its subject not written. m ḥtp 'in peace'. The ba, the self that moves freely after death, must be able to leave the body and to return to it.

sentences.l: spell · of · not · letting · be-repelled · the-heart · of · the-Osiris · the-scribe · of-the-god's-offerings · of · the-gods · all · Ani · true-of-voice · from-him · in · the-necropolis
sentences.i: Spell for not letting the heart of the Osiris, the scribe of the god's offerings of all the gods, Ani, true of voice, be turned back from him in the necropolis.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ḫr n·f; read ḫr·f. The water n between r and the viper gives no sense: ḫr·f is ḫ and r with ·f, 'from him' (Budge: χer-nef). Spell 30B begins, and Budge's line numerals start again at 1. The papyrus writes rꜣ n tm rdit ḫsf·tw ib n in red, with the name and titles in black. ḫr·f m ẖrt-nṯr and ḏd·f are red again. Budge's red overline starts over the n of ḫr·f, and the whole word is marked red here. tm is t, the sledge tm (U15) and m (Aa15) as complement: the negative verb tm 'not to do', with the infinitive rdit after it, 'not letting'. rdit is the mouth r, the giving hand with its loaf (D37) and t. ḫsf·tw is the spindle ḫsf (U35, as one sign) with t and w: ḫsf 'repel, turn back' with ·tw, the passive sḏm·tw·f after rdi, 'letting (the heart) be turned back'. ib n wsir 'the heart of the Osiris', and sš 'scribe' is the palette (Budge: ān). Budge prints ḥtp and nṯr as two groups, and they are joined here as ḥtp-nṯr 'the god's offerings': the offering-mat ḥtp with t and p, then the flag and the seated god. sš ḥtp-nṯr is Ani's title, 'scribe of the god's offerings'. n nṯrw nbw 'of all the gods': nṯrw is the flag three times with a stroke, and nbw is the basket with plural strokes, agreeing with nṯrw. ꜣny has only two strokes after n here (coded Z4A, approximate). mꜣꜥ-ḫrw 'true of voice' is the plinth mꜣꜥ and the oar ḫrw without the sickle. m ẖrt-nṯr as in Spell 26.

sentences.l: says-he · heart-my · of · mother-my · (twice) · heart-my · of · forms-my
sentences.i: He says: My heart of my mother! (Twice.) My heart of my forms of being!
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ḏd·f in red. ḏd·f 'he says' is the cobra ḏ, the hand d and ·f. The speech is the one written over the weighing of the heart (Plates 3–4), and the notes there explain it word by word. ib·i n mwt·i 'my heart of my mother': mwt·i is the vulture mwt with t, a seated woman and ·i. sp sn 'twice' is the threshing floor with two strokes (coded Z4A, approximate). ḥꜣty·i n ḫprw·i 'my heart of my forms': ḫprw·i is the scarab ḫpr with r, plural strokes for the w and ·i, and Budge restores the seated man. The heart came from the mother and grew with its owner through all his forms of being.

sentences.l: do-not · stand-up · against-me · as · witness
sentences.i: Do not stand up against me as a witness.
sentences.n: As over the weighing scene. m 'do not!' is the owl: the negative imperative. ꜥḥꜥ 'stand up' is the mast ꜥḥꜥ with the arm ꜥ (D36) over the walking legs. r·i 'against me'. m 'as' is the sign m (Aa15). mtr 'witness' is the phallus mt (D53) with t, r, a stroke and two tall strokes (coded Z4A, approximate), with the man with hand to mouth as classifier (Budge here: meteru, 'the judgment').

sentences.l: do-not · oppose · against-me · in · the-tribunal
sentences.i: Do not oppose me in the tribunal.
sentences.n: m 'do not!' is the sign Aa15 here. ḫsf 'oppose' is the spindle (U35) with the low hooked sign as classifier. ḏꜣḏꜣt 'the tribunal' is the fire-drill ḏꜣ (coded U28, approximate) written twice, with a small eared ring between (coded W24, approximate), a barred sign (coded N1, approximate), the seated god and a stroke. No t is printed, and the reading supplies the feminine ending.

sentences.l: do-not · make · hostility-your · against-me · in-the-presence-of · the-keeper · of-the-balance
sentences.i: Do not show your hostility to me in the presence of the keeper of the balance.
sentences.n: m 'do not!' with irt, the eye, r and t: the negatival complement, written with t. rqy·k is r, the hill-slope q and two reeds y, with a cord (coded V1, approximate) and the walking legs as classifiers, and ·k. It is rq 'opposition, hostility', the object of irt, and the two reeds are read with the signs; the copy over the weighing scene has rq·k without them. r·i 'against me' is r with a stroke. No seated man is printed, and the stroke is taken as ·i. m-bꜣḥ 'in the presence of' is m (Aa15) and the phallus bꜣḥ (D53) with the roll. iry mḫꜣt 'the keeper of the balance': iry is the reed, r, two strokes y, the man with a stick (A47) and the roll, and mḫꜣt is the balance itself (U38).

sentences.l: you · ka-my · which-is-in · body-my · Khnum · who-makes-sound · limbs-my
sentences.i: You are my ka, which is in my body, the Khnum who keeps my limbs sound.
sentences.n: As over the weighing scene. ntk 'you' (n, t, k) is the independent pronoun: ntk N 'you are N'. imy 'which is in' is the crossed planks im with m and two strokes y. ẖt·i 'my body' (Budge's line 4 begins with it) is the belly ẖ (coded F32, approximate), t, a stroke and ·i. ḫnmw 'Khnum' is the jug ḫnm with m, and here a seated god with horns (coded C4, approximate), the ram-headed Khnum, follows as classifier, so a name is clearly meant. swḏꜣ 'who keeps sound' is s, w, the fire-drill ḏꜣ (U28, approximate) with ꜣ and the roll: a participle. ꜥwt·i 'my limbs' is the arm ꜥ and t, a small loop (coded Z7, read w) and a stroke, and ·i.

sentences.l: go-forth · for-yourself · to · the-place · good · hasten(?)-we · there
sentences.i: Go forth to the good place to which we hasten(?).
sentences.n: Budge prints pr n·k as one group (per-nek), split here as over the weighing scene. pr is the house pr with r and the walking legs, the imperative of pri 'go forth', and n·k 'for yourself' (water n and ·k) is the dative that often follows a verb of motion in the imperative. It could also be read pr·n·k 'you have gone forth'. r bw nfr 'to the good place': bw is the foot b and a stroke, and nfr is the heart and windpipe. ḥn·n is the wick ḥ before a hoe-like sign (coded U6, approximate) over two water lines n, then the walking legs and water n with plural strokes, ·n 'we'. It is taken as ḥn 'hasten', the hoe-like sign standing for ḥn, with the wick and the water lines as complements (Budge: ḥen-n, 'we advance'). Over the weighing scene the sign is a bundle and the subject is ·i 'I'; here it is 'we'. Both the sign and the sense are uncertain. im 'there' points back to bw nfr: 'to which we hasten'.

sentences.l: do-not · make-foul · name-my · to · the-entourage · who-make · people · in · lifetime
sentences.i: Do not make my name foul to the entourage, who set people in their span of life(?).
sentences.n: m 'do not!' (the owl). sḫnš is the bolt s, ḫ, n and the pool š (coded N37, approximate), with a fish (coded K1, approximate) as classifier. It is the causative of ḫnš 'stink', 'make foul' (Budge: seχenś). Over the weighing scene the same place has s, ḫ and r with a fish. This copy writes the full word, which suggests what is meant there. rn·i 'my name' (r and n, the man with hand to mouth, ·i). n 'to'. šnyt 'the entourage' is the rope šn with n, two reeds, t, a standing man with a staff (coded A21, approximate), the seated man and a stroke as classifiers of people (Budge: Śenit). iryw 'who make' is the eye ir with r, two reeds y, the chick w and a stroke: the plural participle of iri. rmṯ 'people' (r, ṯ, man and woman, stroke). ꜥḥꜥw is the mast ꜥḥꜥ with ꜥ and a round-topped stela (coded O26, approximate) with a stroke: 'lifetime', from ꜥḥꜥ 'stand'. iri X m Y is 'make X into Y, set X in Y', so the šnyt are taken as those who fix how long people live (Budge: 'who make men [to be] in stability'). The sense of the phrase is uncertain. Budge's footnote here, which refers to additions printed elsewhere, is not read as text. To be named ill before the court of the gods was to be harmed there.
